hook.en: A man stumbles out of the mist and collapses on the rocks. His face is white, his clothes are a prisoner's. Sadao is a doctor, and also a Japanese patriot.

objectives.en: Narrate how the American is found

narration.en: A man stumbles out of the mist and collapses on the rocks. His face is white, his clothes are a prisoner's. Sadao is a doctor, and also a Japanese patriot.

body.en: One misty evening Sadao and Hana see a man come out of the sea and fall on the rocks. He is a white American, badly wounded, and from his cap and clothes Sadao concludes that he is an American sailor, probably a prisoner of war who has escaped. Handing him over would mean his death; hiding him could mean their own arrest.

points.en: A wounded man on the rocks
Hide him or hand him over?

narration.en: One misty evening Sadao and Hana see a man come out of the sea and fall on the rocks. He is a white American, badly wounded, and from his cap and clothes Sadao concludes that he is an American sailor, probably a prisoner of war who has escaped. Handing him over would mean his death; hiding him could mean their own arrest.
We set out the two sides of Sadao's dilemma.

say.en: We compare As a doctor and As a patriot side by side.
A doctor saves every life; a patriot hands over the enemy.
He has the skill to heal; hiding the man is a crime.
He operates and saves him, but fears arrest.
Humanity wins for now, but loyalty still troubles him.

body.en: Sadao's training as a doctor tells him to save the man; his loyalty to Japan says hand him in. They carry him into the house. Sadao finds a bullet wound and operates to remove the bullet, with Hana helping him despite her fear and disgust. His professional duty wins for the moment.

narration.en: Sadao's training as a doctor tells him to save the man; his loyalty to Japan says hand him in. They carry him into the house. Sadao finds a bullet wound and operates to remove the bullet, with Hana helping him despite her fear and disgust. His professional duty wins for the moment.

problem.en: What was the dilemma faced by Sadao and Hana when they found the American?

steps.en: If they hand him over, he will be killed.
If they hide him, they risk arrest as traitors.
Sadao's duty as a doctor clashes with his duty as a patriot.

answer.en: If they handed the wounded American to the police he would certainly die, but if they sheltered him they could be arrested as traitors. Sadao's duty as a doctor to save life clashed with his loyalty to Japan.
